pr_title: drivers: led_strip: ws2812_spi: Add start/stop frames
pr_body:
Some SPI controllers leave MOSI high when transfer is idle. This corrupts the last and first bit (SPI ZERO or SPI ONE frame) of the pixel transfer since there is no initial low-to-high edge (since MOSI is already high) and an unintended low-to-high edge when transfer is complete.

Adding a SPI byte of 0x00 before and after transfering the pixels, MOSI is forced low for an entire frame before and after pixel transfer.

fixes: #66372
pr_comments:
> Hi @bjarki-trackunit , does this fix #66372 ?

yes, that's the same issue, the extra frame before and after "reset" the bus as described in that PR :)

@simonguinot The issue, that some SPI controllers leave MOSI high after transmission ends, is fixed by sending the start/stop bytes. The fix is quite small and simple so I didn't think to check if there was an existing PR for the same issue, sorry about that.

I see no benefit to introduce pinctrl or SPI configurations when the solution in this PR is simple and essentially free (+2 bytes of RAM)
Hi @IVandeVeire. Please can you verify that this PR fixes your issue ?

Hi @simonguinot . Speaking on behalf of my colleague @IVandeVeire (who's currently sick at home), this PR does not fix our issue. The logic high level resulting from the boot sequence is still misinterpreted as the first part of a data bit (as described in [66372](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/66372)) .

> I see no benefit to introduce pinctrl or SPI configurations when the solution in this PR is simple and essentially free (+2 bytes of RAM)

I agree with you. We've had a lot of issues with the MOSI signal at idle state. So if there is a simple solution which can help everybody at the expense of 2 bytes, then let's go. It is not exactly free as you said (a few bytes sometimes matter), but it is still a good investment.

But is that working ?

@simonguinot This is what I have discovered using my test setup consisting of three leds in series, the yellow line is data in: We are sending GRB, with G=0, R=255 and B=0.

Without the start frame in this PR, the first frame of the transmission is lost, causing a misaligned and corrupted transmission. 
**Data in to first LED (MOSI)**
![nopatch_1_1](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/82143143/f02bb52b-b5ed-4c28-8d0f-99e300d6c3f9)
 **Data from first to second LED**
![nopatch_1_2](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/82143143/af3da58d-80cf-48a0-9182-bda2a18e0aa2)
 **Data from second to thrid LED**
![nopatch_1_3](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/82143143/513feae0-9e4d-4292-8dd2-f80b0a268c7e)
**Data out of third LED**
![nopatch_1_4](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/82143143/15b70faa-788e-4096-a558-e0b9d956537d)
There are supposed to be 24 * 3 frames (bits) sent from MISO, in reality. The first frame is lost due to the MISO being high already, causing a bitshift left of 1 for the entire transmission, meaning we are only sending 29 bits, however, when the MOSI returns to high level after the transmission, we get our last bit, which is always a 1. This is why looking at LEDs 2,3 and out of 3, it looks kind of correct, but we can see that we are actually sending G=1, R=254, B=1. And since we end up sending 30 bits, the last LED sends out nothing.

With the start frame, we get the following:
**Data in to first LED (MOSI)**
![startframe_1_1](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/82143143/008aa4a0-f3a8-4a49-99ef-a7c24c3dd705)
 **Data from first to second LED**
![startframe_1_2](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/82143143/26c1b530-53f7-4ccd-ac41-0315887fff1e)
 **Data from second to thrid LED**
![startframe_1_3](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/82143143/135825a6-f69e-475c-8be3-662ce4aba35f)
**Data out of third LED**
![startframe_1_4](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/82143143/8acb109f-a82f-445c-9a65-44dbcb30ca8d)
We are now sending the correct 30 bits of data, aligned properly, which is seen on the LEDs 1, 2 and 3, but, we are still sending the extra 1, which is why it is sent out of LED3.

Now, it does not actually matter that we are sending the extra 1 since it will always be sent out of the last pixel in the led strip, which is not relevant.

In conclusion, we only need the start byte, we may need more than one depending on the LED variant.

> In conclusion, we only need the start byte, we may need more than one depending on the LED variant.

Thanks for the detailed analysis ! Actually I was thinking that the initial falling edge from idle high to low state was captured as a bit by the first LED controller (shifting everything after). But in your case, it is different: the edge causes the lost of the first bit. So it looks like that the rising edge triggers the capture ? I don't remember very well but I think that in the case of the B1414 controller (WS2812-compatible) the falling edge triggers the capture.

BTW what WS2812-compatible LED controller are you using ? And you @javlands and @IVandeVeire ?

Hi @dleach02,

I don't think so. This fix is not correct. Adding a preamble when the MOSI signal at idle state is high introduces a falling edge which is interpreted as a bit by the first WS2812 controller of the strip. And all the following RGB bits are shifted... For some reason (probably related with the reset state of the LED controller) this helps with the setup used by @bjarki-andreasen. But this doesn't with the one used by @javlands and @IVandeVeire.

IMO, the only way to fix the issue properly is to configure the MOSI signal to be low when idle. The `ws2812_spi` driver is generic and relies on it.

Note that the WS2812 LED strip controller can also be driven through I2S, GPIO, and soon UART too. So if SPI cannot be configured correctly on a platform, there are alternatives.

To elaborate a bit, the fix in this PR is correct, but not sufficient. The WD2812 compatible LEDs I was working with just need a short low period before the first low-to-high edge to register correctly, others evidently don't. I have concluded that SPI controllers which leave MOSI high are simply not generally supported with this driver. So lets just leave the driver as is :)

> To elaborate a bit, the fix in this PR is correct, but not sufficient. The WD2812 compatible LEDs I was working with just need a short low period before the first low-to-high edge to register correctly, others evidently don't.

To elaborate a bit, the period of time the MOSI signal should remain low before transmitting the first RGB bit must be at least the reset delay, which depends on the LED controller model. And 8 SPI clock ticks is arbitrary and just not long enough for most controllers. That's why the patch is not correct to me.

> I have concluded that SPI controllers which leave MOSI high are simply not generally supported with this driver. So lets just leave the driver as is :)

Yes you are right. We can't send a frame with zeros during the entire reset delay. We are no longer speaking of 2 bytes of RAM. So the fix has to come from the SPI side.

issue_context.title: led_strip: ws2812: led strip does misinterpret the logic level that was set during boot as data bits (using LPSPI on RT1064)
issue_context.body: I was asked to create an issue regarding this pr: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/66311 I'm developing an application that uses the ws2812 spi driver to control SK6812-EC3210F addressable leds. I'm using a custom mimx-rt1064 board. I experienced some weird boot behavior of the leds. When the device boots, the bus level of the `mosi` line get to logic high for certain amout of time before sending the first data on the bus. Because the data bits are directly sent after the boot sequence, the leds do misinterpret the logic level that was set during boot as data bits. From my understanding, the `mosi` line keeps the last level that was assigned on the bus when the spi block gets idle. I'm aware that this may be soc specific behaviour. To prevent the led strip from misinterpreting the logic level that was set during boot as data bits, I added a reset after the initialization of the ws2812 driver (as in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/66311 ). I made some captures (of the `mosi` line) using a logic analyzer to clarify the issue. Device boot without fix: Device boot without fix (detailled): Device boot without delay and reset at init:

review_comments: Since we ensure that the signal is low before sending the data, why do we need to set it low after the transmission ?

Because the low-to-high edge occurs right after the last frame, which some (the leds I have) detect as the start of another bit since the edge is within the T1+T0 time. This is received as a 1 bit (since the high edge is longer than T1H), whereas the stop byte ensures the low-to-high edge starts long after T1+T0 (about twice T1+T0)

Oh this is actually a different behavior from the i.MX RT1064 MCU on which the MOSI signal keeps the state of the last sent value (from the logic analyzer capture attached to https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/66372). In your case the signal always returns to a high level just after the transmission and it is interpreted as the next bit.

So what MCU model are you using ? Have you looked if it is possible to change the default level of the MOSI signal ? Maybe via some pinmux configuration ?

Isn't the "long high - low" signal change resulting from this preamble interpreted as a logical "1" by the first LED of the strip? Don't we have to wait for the reset delay before sending data after putting the MOSI signal low ?
The forced low frames are only before and after a complete transmission. The reset delay is between complete transmissions, not each pixel or frame :)

I know that and it is not my question. I'll try to rephrase :) Here we add a 0 byte as a preamble to the data buffer. So I am asking if the first logical bit captured by the first LED of the strip won't be the "high to low" signal transition (probably 1) due to this preamble ?
